qibla.showMap: Show the qibla on a map
qibla.mapLine: The gold line runs from {place} to the Ka'bah, {deg}° from true north. Line yourself up with a street or building edge that runs the same way.

falak.title: Falak
falak.intro: Read the time and the qibla from the sun and its shadow, the way the muwaqqit did. No signal needed.
falak.cameraSub: Qibla and shadow on the camera
falak.neverLook: Never look at the sun, not briefly, not through sunglasses, binoculars or your phone's camera. Look only at the shadow on the ground.
falak.stickShadow: A stick's shadow points {deg}° {point} and is {x}× its height.
falak.sunBelow: The sun is below the horizon.
falak.afterSunrise: Shadow readings start after sunrise. See the sky signs below.
falak.qiblaVsShadow: Shadow points {a} degrees, qibla is {b} degrees
falak.qiblaDayExplain: Twice a year the sun stands directly over the Ka'bah at Makkah noon (istiwa' a'zam). At that minute, every upright shadow wherever the sun is up points straight away from the Ka'bah. It is the most exact qibla check there is, with nothing but a stick.
falak.qiblaDayVisible: Visible from here, the sun will be {deg}° up. Stand a straight stick upright on level ground and face from the shadow's tip to its base. The day before and after also work within about half a degree.
falak.qiblaDayDown: The sun is down here at that moment. Use the daily rashdul qiblat below, or the next Qibla Day.
falak.rashdulExplain: The moments the sun lines up with the qibla from where you are, so any upright shadow lies along the qibla line.
falak.rashdulNone: No alignment with the sun high enough today. Next is {date} at {time}.
falak.rashdulNever: The sun doesn't line up with the qibla from here in the coming weeks. Use the compass or Qibla Day.
falak.rashdulGood: Good for about 2 minutes either side. Check that the stick is truly vertical with a plumb line or a hanging string.
falak.stickHow: Stand a straight stick upright on level ground. A pen on a table works. Measure the stick and its shadow in centimetres.
falak.zawalExplain: {name} begins once the shadow stops shrinking and starts to grow. Asr begins when the shadow is the noon shadow plus the stick's height (twice it, for Hanafi).
falak.yourTimetable: Your timetable has {name} at {dhuhr} and Asr at {asr}. Timetables add a few minutes of ihtiyat (precaution) on top of the sun's geometry.
falak.sunByShadow: The sun is {deg}° up by your shadow.
falak.sunTime: That puts the sun's time at {time} (about {n} min either way), which {result}.
falak.usualCauses: Usual causes are a stick that isn't vertical, ground that isn't level, or a shadow tip that was hard to see. Try again with a plumb line.
falak.tooLow: The sun never gets that low on this side of noon today. Measure again, or check the time.
falak.asrBegun: Asr ({school}) has begun by your shadow. It is past {length}.
falak.asrNotBegun: Asr ({school}) hasn't begun by your shadow. It needs to reach {length}.
falak.morning: Morning reading, before zawal. {name} has not begun.
falak.skyIntro: What the prayer times describe, so you can see them for yourself. For information only, since city lights, haze and buildings hide these signs, and scholars differ on how to read dawn and twilight. Pray by your timetable.
falak.signMaghrib: The whole disc of the sun has gone below the horizon and its upper edge has disappeared. Best seen over the sea or open land. Behind hills or buildings it vanishes early, so don't pray by that.
falak.signIsha: The red glow (shafaq ahmar) has gone from the western sky. This is the view of the Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools. Imam Abu Hanifah held it is the white glow that follows it. Timetables use the sun's depth below the horizon (about 17° to 18°) instead.
falak.signFajr: True dawn (fajr sadiq) is a thin whiteness spreading sideways along the eastern horizon, growing steadily. It is not the false dawn (fajr kazib) before it, a faint upright column of light that fades again. Researchers still debate the exact depth of the sun at true dawn, so this stays for information only.
falakTools.cameraHelp: This view draws the qibla and the stick's shadow over the camera. Allow the camera, or use the compass and the cards on the Falak tab.
falakTools.pointFloor: Point the camera at the floor in front of you.
falakTools.noCompass: No compass on this device, so the lines can't turn with you.
falakTools.darkBar: Dark bar shows where a stick's shadow falls right now
falakTools.outdoors: Outdoors in sunshine, real shadows should lie along the dark bar. If they don't, move away from metal and wave the phone in a figure 8 to calibrate the compass again. Never look at the sun.
falakTools.motionAsk: This browser asks before sharing motion.
falakTools.notLevel: Not level yet. Adjust until the bubble turns green
falakTools.noMotion: This device has no motion sensor.
falakTools.groundHow: Lay the phone flat where the stick will stand. Within 0.5° is good.
falakTools.stickHow: Hold the phone's long edge against the stick. Within 0.5° of vertical is good.
falakTools.tilt: A tilt of 1° moves a 1 m stick's shadow tip by about 1.7 cm, enough to shift a reading by a minute.

settings.berbukaAlertSub: A notification at {name} when it is time to break your fast.

settings.wakeUpFoot: Also on the Prayer screen. Tap the alarm clock at the top.

settings.travelFoot: Jamak and qasar guidance, combined prayer windows and a log of where you've prayed. We'll ask when you land in another country.
settings.calculationFoot: Automatic follows the country you're in, so landing in a new country switches it for you.
settings.subscribeSub: The official {name} times as a calendar feed
settings.add30: Add the next 30 days to a calendar
settings.add30Sub: An .ics file with an alert at every prayer, for {place}
settings.workCalendarSub: So meetings and classes don't land on prayer time. Add it to Outlook or Google Calendar at work.
settings.printSub: A monthly or Ramadan timetable, a sticker calendar or a kids' prayer tracker
settings.letter: Print a letter for work or school
settings.letterSub: Explains your prayer breaks to an employer or teacher, with today's times
settings.namesFoot: Automatic shows English names like Fajr and Isha, or your browser's language if we have it. Pick Malay for Subuh and Isyak. Your names stay the same wherever you go. When you travel somewhere that uses other words, the local name shows small underneath, like Subuh in Kuala Lumpur, so the masjid's signs make sense. Spellings follow each authority's own timetable.
settings.hadithFoot: Tap ✕ on any hadith to hide just that one. Turn both off for a clean app with times only.
settings.showHadithSub: A short hadith or ayah on some screens
settings.wakeHadith: Add a hadith to wake up alerts
settings.wakeHadithSub: One short line under the Fajr and tahajjud alerts
settings.trackerFoot: Tap a prayer on the Prayer screen once it has passed to tick it off, and keep a streak. Tap the streak to mark a day as excused (haid, illness) so it carries on. Kept only in this browser.
settings.nudgeSub: One gentle alert about 30 minutes before a prayer's time ends, only if you haven't ticked it. Not for {name}, which stays open until {until}. Never while paused.
settings.languageFoot: The words on every screen. Prayer names have their own setting.
settings.biggerTextSub: Makes every word and time larger. For the clearest screen, pick Big and Simple as the Prayer screen too.
settings.openingSub: The moving dial you see as the app opens. Turn it off to go straight to your prayer times. It always shows the first time.
settings.alertsFoot: Prayer time alerts ring at the exact time of each prayer you choose. Reminder before prayer gives you a heads up a few minutes earlier (15 by default), so a meeting or work doesn't run past it. Turn on either or both.
settings.alertsWeb: On the web, they ring only while Prayer Times Asia is open, in a tab or as an installed app. For alerts when it's closed, add the times to your calendar above. Your calendar rings them, reminder included.
settings.blocked: Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings.
settings.quietFoot: For shift workers sleeping in the day, a baby asleep in the room, or simply a calm night. Alerts still come, but they only buzz. {name} keeps its sound so it can wake you.
settings.jumuahFoot: A reminder on Fridays to get ready and leave in time. It uses your masjid's own {jumuah} time when you have set one in the Masjid tab, otherwise the start of {dhuhr}. {friday} is not required of women, travellers or the sick, who pray {prayer} instead.
jumuah.ringAlarmSub: Rings like your other alarms, not a quiet notification
jumuah.foot: A reminder on Fridays to get ready and leave in time. It counts back from {from}.
jumuah.footSg: Only some masjids in Singapore hold a second session. The Masjid tab shows which ones.
jumuah.footWho: {friday} is not required of women, travellers or the sick, who pray {dhuhr} instead.
settings.movingFoot: Your places, choices and tracker history travel inside a QR code or link. No account, nothing uploaded. It works between the web, iPhone and Android.
settings.installFoot: Installed, it opens like an app from your Home Screen or dock, works offline, and on iPhone it is the only way the web can show alerts.
settings.addHome: Add Prayer Times Asia to your Home Screen
settings.accuracyFoot: Every day shows its source grade. A is official, B is confirmed by a masjid, C is checked by the community, D is calculated. F (falak) marks a reading from your own shadow stick, which only checks the times. In Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia the app downloads the official MUIS, JAKIM or Kemenag timetable for the year (only the year, zone code or regency name is sent) and keeps it in this browser for offline use. If an authority is down, the app's own calendar feeds (built weekly from the same tables) stand in. Everywhere else, and before that download, times are calculated in your browser with the country's own method, the same engine as the iPhone app, checked against every day of the 2026 MUIS, JAKIM and Kemenag timetables. For Singapore it is never earlier than the official time (at most 2 minutes later). For Malaysia and Indonesia it is within about 2 minutes.
settings.privacy1: No outside ads, no accounts, no tracking across other apps or sites.
settings.privacy2: Your exact location stays in this browser. The place name comes from a built in list, not a server.
settings.usageSub: Tells us how many people use the app and in which city and country, so we know where to add official timetables. A random number stands in for you. No name, no exact location, no IP address kept.
settings.osm: The Masjid map and list use OpenStreetMap data. The map tiles, our weekly masjid list on GitHub and Overpass see only the area you look at.
settings.makersFoot: Prayer Times Asia is free and built fisabilillah in Singapore by Ustaz Aarif Raziff and Ustazah Nasibah Hamzah, with Nasar Digital (Nasar Pte Ltd). The only offers you will see are our own. No ad networks, nothing tracked.
settings.showOffers: Show offers on Prayer and Masjid
settings.helpFoot: A short tour that taps the real buttons, so you know where everything is.
settings.picksFoot: Barakah Picks is not a normal ad. It is one small space we check by hand for halal Muslim businesses and causes, safe for the whole family. No gambling, alcohol, riba or anything immodest, and never Google, Facebook or Instagram ads. Most picks are our own services, and paid ones are marked Sponsored. We keep only simple counts of how often each card is seen and tapped, never who you are.

source.title: Source
source.differ: These two sources differ by more than 2 minutes. We show both rather than silently pick one. Follow your local masjid's practice.
source.jamaahHelp: Prayer time begins at the times on the Prayer screen. These are when the congregation prays.
source.helpVerifySub: Send a masjid timetable, the method masjids here use, or an azan time you heard
source.checked: Submissions are checked by a person before they change anyone's times, and shared openly under CC BY 4.0.
calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.explain: Countries can start Ramadan and celebrate Eid on different days, because of local moon sighting and different methods. Pick whose announcement your masjid follows.
calendar.estimateExplain: Astronomical estimate (Umm al Qura calendar). Local dates may differ by a day.
calendar.notYet: {name} hasn't announced yet. It usually does the evening before. This page updates within a few hours.
calendar.sanad: Every date shows who set it and how, by moon sighting, by calculation, or by following another authority. Dates are shared openly under CC BY 4.0.
journey.setHomeHelp: Tell us where home is and we'll work out when you count as a traveller.
journey.fastingHelp: As a traveller you may choose not to fast, and replace the day after Ramadan. If fasting is easy, fasting is better. The day counts as travel when you left home before Fajr. Mark it on your Ramadan page so it is counted for you. Ask your local religious authority when unsure.
journey.jamakExplain: Jamak taqdim means praying both in the first prayer's time. Jamak ta'khir means praying both in the second prayer's time.
journey.hanafi: In the Hanafi school the travel distance is about 78 km, for stays of up to 15 days. Prayers are shortened but not joined.
journey.distanceHelp: Most of Southeast Asia uses 81 km, which is two marhalah. Some scholars use 89 km. Pick the one your local religious authority uses.
journey.shafii: In the Shafi'i school this holds for stays of up to 3 days, not counting the day you arrive and the day you leave.
journey.notFatwa: This is general guidance on the traveller's concessions (rukhsah), not a fatwa. When unsure, follow your local religious authority.

alerts.headsUpSub: An extra notification this many minutes before each prayer set to Notify
alerts.headsUpSame: The same for every prayer set to Notify
alerts.eachFoot: Pick Off, Notify or Alarm. Tap Change to choose the exact time. Notify is a notification, quiet when your phone is on silent. Alarm rings until you stop it.
alerts.nudgeSub: A notification about 30 minutes before a prayer's time ends, only if you have not ticked it in your tracker. Not for {name}.
alerts.azanSub: Notifications open with the azan, and the {name} azan at {name}
alerts.buzzSub: Notifications vibrate without sound, all day. Alarms still ring.
alerts.quietSub: Between the times you pick, notifications only vibrate. {name} and alarms keep their sound.
alerts.soundFoot: Buzz only and Quiet hours are for shift workers sleeping in the day, a baby asleep in the room, or a calm night. Alarms keep their sound.
alerts.alarmSoundFoot: Tap a sound to hear it. Every alarm plays this sound.
alerts.add30: Add the next 30 days of alarms to a calendar
alerts.morningsHadith: O Allah, bless my ummah in their early mornings.
alerts.morningsSource: The Prophet ﷺ, narrated by Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi
alerts.dayWhite: White days (13, 14 and 15 of the Hijri month)
alerts.howReminder: How should the reminder reach you?
alerts.notifyTooSub: A notification when {name} begins, as well as the alarm
alerts.allowHow: Allow them in your browser's site settings, the icon left of the address.
alerts.addHome: Add the app to your Home Screen
alerts.addHomeSub: On iPhone and iPad, the web can only show alerts from the Home Screen.
alerts.stayOpenSub: On the web, alerts and alarms ring only while Prayer Times Asia is open, in a tab or as an installed app.
alerts.silent: Silent mode and Do Not Disturb
alerts.silentSub: Web notifications stay quiet then. Only the phone app's alarms ring through.
alerts.makeAlarmSub: Make it an alarm so it rings out loud.
alerts.appSub: Alarms that ring on silent, even with the app closed
notify.nudgeBody: {name} is open until {time}. Tick it in the app once you have prayed.
notify.qiyamTitle: Night {night} · the last third has begun
notify.qiyamOdd: An odd night of the last ten. Seek Lailatul Qadr.
notify.qiyamEven: One of the last ten nights of Ramadan.
journey.homeBody: Pray in full. Travel concessions apply once you journey at least {km} km.
journey.nearbyBody: That's short of the travel distance, so pray in full.
journey.travellerBody: You may shorten (qasar) and join (jamak) your prayers. Here is what changes for each one.
journey.travellerHanafi: You may shorten (qasar) your prayers. In the Hanafi school prayers are not joined outside Hajj. Here is what changes for each one.
journey.settledBody: You've been here {n} days. Staying longer than {max} days ends the travel concession, so pray in full.
journey.notTravel: You are {km} km from home. That is less than {limit} km, so this trip does not count as travel yet.
journey.isTravel: You are {km} km from home. That is more than {limit} km, so this trip counts as travel.
masjid.locationOff: Location is turned off for this site. Showing places near {place}.
masjid.locationFailed: Couldn't find where you are. Showing places near {place}.
masjid.driveNote: Drive times are a rough guide. Your maps app shows the traffic, so a masjid a little further away may be quicker.
masjid.choosePlaceBody: Tap the button above, or pick a city on the Prayer tab.
masjid.nothingOpenBody: Only places with opening hours on the map count here. Turn off Open now only to see the rest.
masjid.secondFridayWomen: Second Friday prayer from {time}, with space for women.
masjid.moreOnMap: {n} more within 15 km are on the map. Tap a pin to see its name and directions.
masjid.moreOnMap_one: {n} more within 15 km is on the map. Tap a pin to see its name and directions.
masjid.keepHint: Tap a place and choose Make it my masjid to keep it at the top.
masjid.mapCredit: Places from OpenStreetMap, kept by volunteers. Missing one, or a pin in the wrong spot? {link}, no sign up needed.
masjid.noFacilities: The map doesn't list this place's facilities yet.
masjid.iqamahHow: Iqamah times show here when your masjid puts up a Prayer Times Asia screen. Scan its QR code once.
masjid.eidNearest: {date}. Prayer times at the masjids nearest you.
masjid.fromMuis: From the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS). {link}
masjid.fromMuisUpdated: From the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), updated {date}. No booking needed, except on public holidays. {link}
masjid.fridayHold: {n} masjids hold a second Friday prayer from {time}, for those who can't make the first one at {name}.
masjid.women2: Space for women in the 2nd prayer
feedback.title: A note to the makers
feedback.intro: Ustaz Aarif and the Nasar Digital team read every note. Good or bad, it helps us make the app better for everyone.
feedback.kindHint: What has the app helped you with?
feedback.ideaHint: What would make the app better for you?
feedback.timeHint: Which prayer, which day, and what does your masjid show?
feedback.brokeHint: What did you tap, and what happened?
feedback.addDetails: Add my city and app version
feedback.addDetailsSub: Helps us check your times. Never your exact location.
feedback.mayShareSub: On our website, without your name.
feedback.copy: No email app? Copy the note
feedback.goesTo: It goes to {email}. We reply within a few days, insha Allah.
review.title: Rate and review
review.intro: A few honest words help other Muslims find the app, and help Ustaz Aarif and the team keep going. Jazakallahu khairan.
review.step1: {b} in the box below, in your own words.
review.step2: {b} to review. We copy your words for you.
review.step3: {b} in their review box, then {paste}. Come back and do the same for the next one.
review.copiedHow: Copied. Tap and hold in the review box, then Paste.
review.private: Something not right? Send a private note
review.googleSub: The team in Singapore who builds the app
source.feedDetail: Published by the authority and loaded through Prayer Times Asia's own calendar feed, which a workflow rebuilds every week from the official table. Kept in this browser, so it works offline.
source.downloadedDetail: Downloaded once a year from the authority and kept in this browser, so it works offline.
source.sunriseCalculated: {name} is not in the feed, so it is calculated (never later than the official time).
notify.testBody: This is how prayer alerts will look on this device.
alerts.ramadanFoot: These are notifications, so they stay quiet on silent. Ramadan follows the date in the app. Please follow your local religious authority.
alerts.movesWith: The time moves a little each day with {name}.
alerts.bigAlarm: Your {name} alarm rings {when} at this time
alerts.bigNotify: Your {name} notification comes {when} at this time
